nodes_add.name: Akshay Kumar Datta
nodes_add.note: Rationalist writer; edited the Tattvabodhini Patrika from 1843; led the radical Brahmos who pressed Debendranath to abandon Vedic infallibility (c. 1847-1850). Birth/death years from general knowledge, not rechecked this batch

nodes_add.name: Sadharan Brahmo Samaj
nodes_add.note: Founded 15 May 1878 by Sivanath Sastri, Ananda Mohan Bose and others who left Keshab after the Cooch Behar marriage; constitution with adult franchise

nodes_add.name: Thomas Paine
nodes_add.note: English-born radical; Phule read Rights of Man in 1847 and named Paine as an influence

nodes_update.name: Debendranath Tagore
nodes_update.note: Born 15 May 1817, Jorasanko; Tattvabodhini Sabha 6 Oct 1839; Brahmo covenant 21 Dec 1843 (7 Pous 1765 Shaka); four students to Benares 1845; Vedic infallibility abandoned c. 1847-1850; Brahmo Dharma (1848-1854 in different sources); Adi Brahmo Samaj after 1866; Santiniketan lease 1863 (Visva-Bharati; 1867 in Banglapedia and Wikipedia); Anglo-Hindu College 1827 or 1829; died 19 Jan 1905

nodes_update.name: Keshab Chandra Sen
nodes_update.note: Born 19 Nov 1838, Calcutta; joined Brahmo Samaj 1857 (some say 1859); acharya 1862; Brahmo Samaj of India 11 or 15 Nov 1866; lecture on Jesus Christ May 1866; England 1870; Act III of 1872; Cooch Behar marriage 1878; Nava Vidhan Jan 1880 (1881 in some sources); died 8 Jan 1884

nodes_update.name: Jyotirao Phule
nodes_update.note: Mali caste, Poona; girls' school 1848; Gulamgiri June 1873; Satyashodhak Samaj 24 Sept 1873; one Creator (Nirmik) without mediators; titled Mahatma 11 May 1888; died 28 Nov 1890

edges_upsert.note: Brahmo Sabha, revived by Debendranath as the Brahmo Samaj; Debendranath's father Dwarkanath was a trustee (1830)
Bengali Katha Upanishad 1840; Brahmo Dharma compiled mainly from Upanishadic passages
Banglapedia: the radical section led by Akshay Kumar Datta questioned Vedic infallibility before the leadership abandoned it c. 1847
Keshab joined Debendranath's Samaj 1857; installed as acharya 1862; withdrew Feb 1865; founded Brahmo Samaj of India Nov 1866. Replaces earlier 'lived-with' type, which is not supported
Father; Rabindranath founded his school at Debendranath's Santiniketan ashram
Lecture 'Jesus Christ: Europe and Asia' (1866); Christ central to the New Dispensation, though he never converted; Eucharist adapted with rice and water
Founded 15 May 1878 by followers who left Keshab over the Cooch Behar marriage
Narendranath joined the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj as a student (per vivekananda.mdx)
Mission school 1841-1847; Omvedt notes he called Christ the 'Bali of the West'
Read Rights of Man in 1847 (Pune University Phule Chair life sketch)
Ambedkar named Phule among his three gurus and dedicated Who Were the Shudras? (1946) 'to the Memory of Mahatma Jotiba Fule'

glossary.def: In the Brahmo Samaj, the minister who leads congregational worship; more widely, a teacher.
The 'original' Brahmo Samaj, Debendranath Tagore's body after Keshab Chandra Sen's group left in 1865-66.
The New Dispensation, Keshab Chandra Sen's church (1880 or 1881), which treated all religions as parts of one continuing revelation.
The Society of Truth-Seekers, founded by Jotirao Phule in Poona in 1873 against caste and priestly mediation.
Phule's name for God: the Creator, worshipped directly by everyone without a priest.

issues: debendranath-tagore.mdx: could not access the text of the Autobiography's Chapter I (Gutenberg and archive.org blocked); the grandmother's deathbed and Isha Upanishad page episodes are given from secondary sources and paraphrased, with the date of the grandmother's death as 1835 or 1838. Check against the Autobiography, ch. 1-2.

debendranath-tagore.mdx: Brahmo Dharma date varies (1848, 1849, 1850, 1854, and 1869 for the Rig Veda material in Banglapedia); Santiniketan given as 1863 (Visva-Bharati) against 1867 in Banglapedia; the text follows Visva-Bharati.
debendranath-tagore.mdx: his views on maya, monism and avatars are taken from Evelyn Underhill's 1914 introduction; a primary citation from Brahmo Dharma or his sermons would be better.

keshab-chandra-sen.mdx: Nava Vidhan dated January 1880 (Banglapedia 'Brahma Sabha') or 1881 (Banglapedia 'Sen, Keshab Chandra'; New International Encyclopaedia); daughter's age 13 or 14; birthplace Calcutta vs Garifa; join date 1857 vs 1859. All hedged in the text.
keshab-chandra-sen.mdx: grandfather Ramkamal Sen's opposition to Rammohan rests on Wikipedia only; the 1866 Brahmo Samaj of India founding is 15 November in Banglapedia and 11 November elsewhere.

keshab-chandra-sen.mdx: no verbatim quotation from Keshab's own lectures could be fetched (archive.org blocked); the teaching section paraphrases. A short quote from 'Asia's Message to Europe' would strengthen it.
jyotirao-phule.mdx: birthplace given as Poona; some accounts name the family's village (Katgun, Satara) instead; not checked. The wedding-procession insult (1848) is his own later account.

Possible new edge jyotirao-phule -> dayananda-saraswati (Phule protected Dayananda's Poona procession, 5 Sept 1875, per Forward Press 2026). Not added, since it is not an influence; the author may want a 'protected' edge.
Bhide Wada and Phule Wada coordinates are approximate and marked unverified.

factcheck: Debendranath's grandmother episode and Isha page could not be read in the Autobiography body (nvli PDF holds only Underhill's introduction and the translator's chapter); hedged as his autobiography 'as summarised by later writers'. Banglapedia gives 1838 for the grandmother's death; Wikipedia garbles it as the grandfather.

factcheck: Debendranath's Himalayan retreat: translator's chapter says from 1856, about a year and a half near Simla; Underhill's introduction says he set out in Ashwin 1857 and travelled about three years. Text now gives both.

factcheck: Keshab's grandfather Ramkamal Sen as an opponent of Rammohan still rests on Wikipedia ('lifelong opponent'); Banglapedia is silent. Hedged as 'by some accounts'. A scholarly source (Kopf or Stevens) would settle it.
factcheck: Phule's 1848 school: Pune University Phule Chair says it was for Shudra and Atishudra girls; other accounts say girls of all castes. Text gives both.

joined 1857; acharya 1862; Brahmo Samaj of India 15 Nov 1866; 101 branches by 1872; England March-Sept 1870; Act III 1872; Cooch Behar Feb 1878 'providential'; Nava Vidhan 1881; Ramakrishna 1875-84; motherhood of God, yoga, vairagya -> https://en.banglapedia.org/index.php/Sen,_Keshab_Chandra

jyotirao-phule: born 11 April 1827; married 1840; schools 1834-38 and 1841-47; Paine 1847; 1848 insult and girls' school; left home 1849; schools 1851; infanticide home 1863; well 1868; municipality 1876-82; Gulamgiri June 1873; Shetkaryacha Asud 18 July 1883; Mahatma 11 May 1888; Sarvajanik Satya Dharma begun 1889, posthumous; died 28 Nov 1890 -> https://unipune.ac.in/chairs/mahatma_phule_chair/mphule_webfiles/life_sketch.htm

Satyashodhak 24 Sept 1873; first president; Nirmik without mediator; Satyadipika Oct 1873, ~700 families; weddings without Brahmins -> https://www.forwardpress.in/2014/09/saluting-satyashodak-samajs-pioneering-work/

inverted Aryan conquest theory; avatars as invasion stages; Bali ideal king; Christ 'Bali of the West' -> https://caravanmagazine.in/vantage/gail-omvedts-writing-jotirao-phule-kingdom-mahabali-excerpt
